questions.prompt: Which SQL clause returns only rows that have matching values in both tables?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns only rows that have matching values in both tables.

questions.prompt: When using a LEFT JOIN, which rows are guaranteed to appear in the result set?

options.text: Only rows with matches in both tables
Rows from the left table with or without matches in the right table
Only rows from the right table with matches
Rows from the right table with or without matches

questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN always returns all rows from the left table, regardless of matches in the right table.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly performs a self join to list employees and their managers?

options.text: SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id
SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.id = m.manager_id
SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e RIGHT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id
SELECT e.name, m.name FROM employees e FULL JOIN employees m ON e.id = m.manager_id

questions.explanation: The ON clause e.manager_id = m.id correctly links each employee to their manager.

questions.prompt: Which result set will a FULL OUTER JOIN produce compared to an INNER JOIN?

options.text: Only rows that exist in both tables
All rows from both tables, matching where possible
Only rows from the left table
Only rows from the right table

questions.explanation: A FULL OUTER JOIN returns all rows from both tables, filling unmatched columns with NULLs.
